```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 5.5,
  dpi = 150
)

# In the PDF, scale every chart to the width of the text
if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(out.width = "100%")
}

.old_plot_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("plot")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) {
  out <- .old_plot_hook(x, options)
  if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    out <- paste0('<div class="plot-frame">\n', out, '\n</div>')
  }
  out
})

library(here)
source(here("R", "load_packages.R"))
source(here("R", "config.R"))
source(here("R", "theme.R"))
source(here("R", "get_data.R"))
source(here("R", "process.R"))

refresh <- isTRUE(params$refresh_data)
```

```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
# Downloads happen only on the first knit or when refresh_data is true.
pep_long   <- load_pep(refresh)
components <- load_components(refresh)
shapes     <- tryCatch(load_shapes(refresh), error = function(e) {
  warning(conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE); NULL })
decennial  <- tryCatch(load_decennial(refresh), error = function(e) {
  warning(conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE); NULL })
acs_raw    <- tryCatch(load_acs(refresh), error = function(e) {
  warning(conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE); NULL })

places     <- make_place_lookup(pep_long)
geo_labels <- make_geo_labels(pep_long, places)
annual     <- build_annual(pep_long)
benchmarks <- build_benchmarks(pep_long)
growth     <- build_growth(pep_long, pep_vintage)
comp       <- build_components(components)
dec        <- build_decennial(decennial)
acs        <- build_acs_indicators(acs_raw)

focus          <- filter(places, focus)
kingston_geoid <- focus %>% filter(name == "Kingston city") %>% pull(geoid)
county_geoids  <- paste0(state_fips, study_counties)
home_geoid     <- paste0(state_fips, study_counties[[home_county]])

# Focus places ordered from largest to smallest, for facets and tables
focus_order <- annual %>%
  filter(geoid %in% focus$geoid, year == max(year)) %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  left_join(select(places, geoid, label), by = "geoid") %>%
  pull(label)

first_or_na <- function(x) if (length(x) > 0) x[[1]] else NA
kingston_latest <- annual %>% filter(geoid == kingston_geoid, year == pep_vintage) %>%
  pull(population) %>% first_or_na()
kingston_growth <- filter(growth, geoid == kingston_geoid)
kingston_2020 <- first_or_na(kingston_growth$census_2020)
kingston_2010 <- first_or_na(kingston_growth$pop_2010)
```

# About this report

This report tracks the population of the City of Kingston and the towns around
it, using four Census Bureau sources: annual population estimates for cities
and towns, county estimates of births, deaths and migration, the decennial
census, and the American Community Survey (ACS). The Kingston area here means
`r knitr::combine_words(focus_order)`. Maps cover every city and town in
`r knitr::combine_words(paste(names(study_counties), "County"))`.

The 2020 Census counted `r fmt_count(kingston_2020)` residents in the City of
Kingston, against `r fmt_count(kingston_2010)` in April 2010. The Census Bureau's
most recent estimate, for July 1, `r pep_vintage`, is `r fmt_count(kingston_latest)`.

# Population since 2000

Each line is the Census Bureau's July 1 estimate; the circles are the April 1
benchmarks from the 2000, 2010 and 2020 censuses. The shaded area marks the years since
the 2020 Census, which come from the current estimates series rather than from
the reconciled intercensal series.

```{r annual-focus, fig.height = 9}
label_focus <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    inner_join(select(focus, geoid, label), by = "geoid") %>%
    mutate(label = factor(label, levels = focus_order))
}
focus_annual <- annual %>% label_focus()
focus_bench  <- benchmarks %>% label_focus()

ggplot(focus_annual, aes(date, population)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = as.Date("2020-04-01"), xmax = max(focus_annual$date),
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey60", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(colour = okabe_ito[["blue"]], linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = focus_bench, shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = "black", size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(title = "Population of the Kingston area, 2000-present",
       x = NULL, y = "Residents",
       caption = paste0("Sources: Census Bureau intercensal estimates 2000-2010 and 2010-2020; ",
                        vintage_label, " estimates. Each panel has its own vertical scale.")) +
  theme_kingston()
```

# Kingston in context

Population indexed to July 2010 = 100, so places of very different size can be
compared on one scale.

```{r index-plot}
index_geoids <- c(kingston_geoid, county_geoids, state_fips)

idx <- annual %>%
  filter(geoid %in% index_geoids, year >= 2010) %>%
  group_by(geoid) %>%
  mutate(index = 100 * population / first_or_na(population[year == 2010])) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(geo_labels, by = "geoid") %>%
  mutate(is_kingston = geoid == kingston_geoid)

idx_end <- idx %>% group_by(geoid) %>% filter(year == max(year)) %>% ungroup()

index_colours <- setNames(
  c(okabe_ito[["vermillion"]], okabe_ito[["blue"]], okabe_ito[["green"]],
    okabe_ito[["purple"]], "grey40")[seq_along(index_geoids)],
  geo_labels$label[match(index_geoids, geo_labels$geoid)]
)

ggplot(idx, aes(year, index, colour = label, group = label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2020, colour = "grey50", linetype = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(linewidth = is_kingston)) +
  geom_point(data = idx_end, size = 1.8) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = idx_end, aes(label = label), hjust = 0,
                           nudge_x = 0.4, direction = "y", size = 3.2,
                           segment.colour = "grey60", min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = index_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1.3, `FALSE` = 0.7), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, pep_vintage, 5),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.25))) +
  labs(title = "Population growth since 2010",
       x = NULL, y = "Index (July 2010 = 100)",
       caption = paste0("Sources: Census Bureau intercensal estimates 2010-2020; ",
                        vintage_label, " estimates.")) +
  theme_kingston()
```

# Growth before and after 2020

Average annual growth, compounded, over two periods: the decade between the
2010 and 2020 censuses, and the years since. Each period is measured within a
single Census series, so the change of series in 2020 does not distort it.

```{r growth-table}
growth_rows <- growth %>%
  filter(geoid %in% c(focus$geoid, county_geoids, state_fips)) %>%
  left_join(geo_labels, by = "geoid") %>%
  mutate(order = case_when(
    sumlev == "061" ~ match(label, focus_order),
    sumlev == "050" ~ 100L + match(geoid, county_geoids),
    TRUE            ~ 200L
  )) %>%
  arrange(order)

growth_rows %>%
  transmute(
    Place = label,
    `April 2010` = fmt_count(pop_2010),
    `April 2020 (census)` = fmt_count(census_2020),
    !!paste("July", pep_vintage, "estimate") := fmt_count(pop_latest),
    `Annual growth 2010-2020` = fmt_rate(cagr_2010_2020),
    !!paste0("Annual growth 2020-", pep_vintage) := fmt_rate(cagr_2020_latest)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r growth-map, eval = !is.null(shapes), fig.height = 7}
growth_long <- growth %>%
  select(geoid, cagr_2010_2020, cagr_2020_latest) %>%
  pivot_longer(-geoid, names_to = "period", values_to = "cagr") %>%
  mutate(period = factor(
    if_else(period == "cagr_2010_2020", "April 2010 to April 2020",
            paste("April 2020 to July", pep_vintage)),
    levels = c("April 2010 to April 2020", paste("April 2020 to July", pep_vintage))
  ))

growth_map <- shapes$cousub %>% inner_join(growth_long, by = c("GEOID" = "geoid"))

# Cap the colour scale so one tiny town with an extreme rate does not wash
# out the rest of the map; capped values show in the darkest colour.
lim <- quantile(abs(growth_map$cagr), 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(growth_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = cagr), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = shapes$counties, fill = NA, colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(growth_map, GEOID == kingston_geoid),
          fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ period) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = 1, limits = c(-lim, lim),
                       oob = scales::squish, name = "Average annual change (%)") +
  labs(title = "Where the area grew and shrank",
       caption = paste0("City of Kingston outlined in black. Red = decline, blue = growth. ",
                        "Sources: Census Bureau intercensal estimates; ", vintage_label, " estimates.")) +
  theme_kingston_map() +
  theme(legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))
```

# What is driving change in `r home_county` County

The Census Bureau splits each county's population change into natural change
(births minus deaths), net domestic migration (moves to and from other U.S.
counties, including New York City), and net international migration. These
figures exist for counties only, not for cities and towns.

```{r components-home}
home_comp <- comp %>% filter(geoid == home_geoid)

home_bars <- home_comp %>%
  select(year, NATURALCHG, DOMESTICMIG, INTERNATIONALMIG) %>%
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "component", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(component = factor(component,
    levels = c("NATURALCHG", "DOMESTICMIG", "INTERNATIONALMIG"),
    labels = c("Natural change (births minus deaths)", "Net domestic migration",
               "Net international migration")))

year_levels <- as.character(sort(unique(home_comp$year)))
series_break <- match("2020", year_levels) + 0.5

ggplot(home_bars, aes(factor(year, levels = year_levels), value, fill = component)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  geom_point(data = home_comp,
             aes(factor(year, levels = year_levels), NPOPCHG),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 23, fill = "white", size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = series_break, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(okabe_ito[c("vermillion", "blue", "green")]), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(title = paste0(home_county, " County: sources of population change"),
       subtitle = "Diamonds show the total change, which also includes a residual the Census Bureau cannot assign to a component",
       x = "Twelve months ending June 30", y = "People",
       caption = paste0("Sources: Census Bureau Vintage 2020 estimates (to the dashed line) and ",
                        vintage_label, " estimates (after it). The two series are not reconciled.")) +
  theme_kingston()
```

```{r components-compare, fig.height = 5}
post_label <- paste0("2021-", pep_vintage)

rates <- comp %>%
  filter(geoid %in% c(paste0(state_fips, comparison_counties), state_fips)) %>%
  mutate(period = case_when(year <= 2019 ~ "2011-2019",
                            year >= 2021 ~ post_label)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(period)) %>%
  group_by(geoid, name, period) %>%
  summarise(
    `Net domestic migration`      = 1000 * sum(DOMESTICMIG) / sum(POPESTIMATE),
    `Net international migration` = 1000 * sum(INTERNATIONALMIG) / sum(POPESTIMATE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("Net"), names_to = "component", values_to = "rate")

name_order <- rates %>%
  filter(period == post_label, component == "Net domestic migration") %>%
  arrange(rate) %>% pull(name)

rates <- rates %>% mutate(name = factor(name, levels = name_order))

ggplot(rates, aes(rate, name)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(aes(group = name), colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = period), size = 2.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ component) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("grey45", okabe_ito[["vermillion"]]),
                                        c("2011-2019", post_label)),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Migration rates before and after 2020",
       x = "Average per year, per 1,000 residents", y = NULL,
       caption = "Sources: Census Bureau Vintage 2020 and current-vintage county estimates.") +
  theme_kingston()
```

```{r housing-scatter, eval = !is.null(dec), fig.height = 6.5}
dec_years <- sort(unique(dec$year))
y0 <- min(dec_years); y1 <- max(dec_years)

dec_change <- dec %>%
  filter(year %in% c(y0, y1)) %>%
  select(geoid, year, population, housing_units) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = c(population, housing_units)) %>%
  mutate(
    pop_change = 100 * (.data[[paste0("population_", y1)]] /
                          .data[[paste0("population_", y0)]] - 1),
    hu_change  = 100 * (.data[[paste0("housing_units_", y1)]] /
                          .data[[paste0("housing_units_", y0)]] - 1)
  ) %>%
  inner_join(select(places, geoid, label, focus), by = "geoid") %>%
  arrange(focus)   # draw the Kingston-area points last, on top

ggplot(dec_change, aes(pop_change, hu_change)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linetype = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = focus), size = 2.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = filter(dec_change, focus), aes(label = label),
                           size = 3.2, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = okabe_ito[["vermillion"]], `FALSE` = "grey55"),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = "Kingston area", `FALSE` = "Other cities and towns"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(title = paste0("Housing units and residents, ", y0, "-", y1),
       subtitle = "Above the dashed line, housing grew faster than population",
       x = "Change in population (%)", y = "Change in housing units (%)",
       caption = "Source: decennial census counts for cities and towns in the study counties.") +
  theme_kingston()
```

```{r persons-per-unit, eval = !is.null(dec)}
dec %>%
  inner_join(select(focus, geoid, label), by = "geoid") %>%
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = focus_order)) %>%
  select(label, year, persons_per_occupied) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = persons_per_occupied) %>%
  arrange(label) %>%
```

# Who lives here

These figures come from the American Community Survey, which samples a small
share of households each year and pools five years of responses for places
this size. Every estimate carries a margin of error; the bars below show 90%
intervals. The periods compared do not overlap, as the Census Bureau advises.

```{r no-acs, eval = is.null(acs), results = "asis"}
cat("*ACS data could not be retrieved, so this section is empty.",
    "Check the Census API key and knit again with `refresh_data: true`.*")
```

```{r acs-setup, eval = !is.null(acs)}
acs_focus <- acs %>%
  inner_join(select(focus, geoid, label), by = "geoid") %>%
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = rev(focus_order)),
         period = factor(period, levels = period_label(acs_years)))

period_colours <- setNames(
  c("grey65", okabe_ito[["skyblue"]], okabe_ito[["blue"]])[seq_along(acs_years)],
  period_label(acs_years)
)
```


Share of residents who lived somewhere else one year earlier. Moves from New
York City count as moves from another New York county.

```{r acs-mobility, eval = !is.null(acs), fig.height = 6}
  ggplot(aes(estimate, label, colour = period)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = pmax(estimate - moe, 0), xmax = estimate + moe),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ indicator) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = period_colours, name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Recent arrivals",
       x = "Share of residents age 1 and over (90% interval)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Source: ACS 5-year estimates, table B07003.") +
```


## Income, rents and home values

Change between the two most recent non-overlapping periods. Dollar figures are
in each period's own (nominal) dollars, so part of every increase is
inflation. An asterisk marks a change that is statistically significant at the
90% level.

```{r acs-change-tables, eval = !is.null(acs), results = "asis"}
from_year <- acs_years[length(acs_years) - 1]
to_year   <- acs_years[length(acs_years)]

change_indicators <- c("Median household income", "Median gross rent",
                       "Median home value", "Median age")

for (ind in change_indicators) {
  fmt <- if (ind == "Median age") function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x) else fmt_money
  # "estimate +/- margin", or a dash where the Census Bureau suppressed the figure
  with_moe <- function(est, moe) {
    if_else(is.na(est), "-", paste0(fmt(est), " &plusmn; ", fmt(moe)))
  }

  tbl <- acs_change(acs, ind, from_year, to_year) %>%
    inner_join(select(focus, geoid, label), by = "geoid") %>%
    mutate(label = factor(label, levels = focus_order)) %>%
    arrange(label) %>%
    transmute(
      Place = label,
      !!period_label(from_year) := with_moe(estimate_from, moe_from),
      !!period_label(to_year)   := with_moe(estimate_to, moe_to),
      Change = if_else(is.na(change), "-",
                       paste0(fmt(change), if_else(coalesce(significant, FALSE), "*", "")))
    )

  print(knitr::kable(tbl, align = "lrrr", caption = ind))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

# Notes on the data

- **Annual estimates** come from the Census Bureau's Population Estimates
  Program. For cities and towns these are modelled, mainly from changes in
  housing units, not counted, and they carry no margin of error. Each new
  vintage revises every year back to the last census. The 2000–2010 and
  2010–2020 series are intercensal estimates, adjusted to agree with the
  census at both ends of the decade; the years since 2020 are
  `r vintage_label` estimates.
- **Components of change** (births, deaths, migration) are produced only for
  counties. Figures before July 2020 come from Vintage 2020, which was not
  revised after the 2020 Census, so the two halves of that chart are not
  perfectly consistent.
- **Decennial census counts** for 2020 include noise added for privacy
  (differential privacy). At the scale of a town the effect on total
  population is small; housing unit totals were not altered.
- **ACS figures** are survey estimates with margins of error at the 90% level.
  Small towns can have wide intervals; a change is reported as significant only
  when it exceeds the combined margin of error of the two periods.
- **Data versions in this report:** `r vintage_label` population estimates;
  ACS 5-year periods `r knitr::combine_words(period_label(acs_years))`;
  boundaries from `r shapes_year`.

# Sources

U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program
(<https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest.html>); 2000, 2010 and 2020
Decennial Census; American Community Survey 5-year estimates; TIGER/Line
cartographic boundary files. Data retrieved with the tidycensus and tigris R
packages.
